'''Hozumi Kui''' (穂積 咋) was a Japanese figure of the {{ill|Asuka period|en|Asuka period|qid=Q210688|lt=Asuka period}}, bearing the {{ill|Kabane|de|Kabane|es|Kabane|fa|کابانه|ff|Kabane|fr|Kabane|he|קאבאנה|id|Kabane|ja|カバネ|ko|성 (씨성제)|nl|Kabane|pt|Kabane|ru|Кабанэ|uk|Кабане (титул)|zh|姓 (日本政治结构)|qid=Q1664099|lt=kabane}} title of {{ill|Omi (title)|en|Omi (title)|qid=Q2574718|lt=Omi}}. In {{ill|645|ab|645|af|645|als|645|am|645 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|645|ar|645|ary|645|ast|645|avk|645|az|645|azb|۶۴۵ (میلادی)|be|645|be_x_old|645|bg|645|bn|৬৪৫|bpy|মারি ৬৪৫|br|645|bs|645.|ca|645|cdo|645 nièng|ceb|645|ckb|٦٤٥|crh|645|cs|645|cv|645|cy|645|da|645|de|645|el|645|eml|645|eo|645|es|645|et|645|eu|645|fa|۶۴۵ (میلادی)|fi|645|fo|645|fr|645|fy|645|ga|645|gan|645年|gd|645|gl|645|he|645|hi|645|hr|645.|ht|645 (almanak jilyen)|hu|645|hy|645|id|645|io|645|it|645|ja|645年|jv|645|ka|645|kk|645 жыл|ko|645년|la|645|lb|645|lij|645|lmo|645|lt|645 m.|map_bms|645|mdf|645|mg|645|mhr|645|mk|645|mr|इ.स. ६४५|mrj|645 и|ms|645|mzn|۶۴۵|nah|645|nap|645|nds|645|new|सन् ६४५|nl|645|nn|645|no|645|nso|645|oc|645|or|୬୪୫|os|645-æм аз|pl|645|pnb|645|pt|645|qu|645|ro|645|ru|645 год|rue|645|sa|६४५|sah|645 сыл|scn|645|sd|645ع|se|645|sh|645.|shn|645|si|645|sk|645|sl|645|sq|645|sr|645|su|645|sv|645|sw|645|tg|Соли 645|th|พ.ศ. 1188|tk|645|tl|645|tly|645|tr|645|tt|645 ел|uk|645|ur|645ء|uz|645|vec|645|vi|645|war|645|wuu|645年|xmf|645|zh|645年|zh_min_nan|645 nî|zh_yue|645年|qid=Q135579113}} (645), he was appointed as the first {{ill|Kokushi (official)|en|Kokushi (official)|qid=Q1351234|lt=Provincial Governor}} of the Eastern Provinces. His {{ill|cap Rank|ja|冠位|lt=Crown Rank}} included {{ill|Koetsuga|ja|小乙下}} and {{ill|Daisenjō|ja|大山上}}.

== Career ==
In Taika 1 (645), Hozumi Kui was dispatched as the first Provincial Governor of the Eastern Provinces. On the 19th day of the 9th month, Emperor Kōtoku issued an edict instructing provincial governors to govern with virtue. However, in Taika 2 (646), reports surfaced of misconduct during Kui's tenure, though he avoided severe punishment due to a general amnesty.

In Taika 5 (650), Kui was tasked by the Emperor to investigate suspicions of treason involving the {{ill|Minister of the Right|en|Minister of the Right|qid=Q1351174|lt=Minister of the Right}}, {{ill|Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro|en|Soga no Kurayamada no Ishikawa no Maro|qid=Q3488899|lt=Soga no Kurayamada Ishikawa Maro}}. Subsequently, Kui joined forces with {{ill|Soga no Hinokuma|ja|蘇我日向}} to lead a military expedition against Ishikawa Maro. The forces surrounded Maro's refuge at {{ill|Yamada-dera|en|Yamada-dera|qid=Q3571406|lt=Yamada-dera}}, where Maro had already taken his own life along with his family. Kui commanded {{ill|Mononobe no Fututa no Shio|ja|物部二田塩}} to decapitate Maro's corpse.
